# Nutrient cycling — carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus

## 1. Introduction
Opening frame for **Nutrient cycling — carbon** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Organisms and Environment fill pass.

## 2. Hierarchy body — every syllabus sub-point
### Nutrient cycling — carbon
### nitrogen
### phosphorus

Fill order per concept: definition → structure → process → significance (§3.2). Step-by-step numbered points, Pioneer style.

Nutrient cycling (biogeochemical cycling) returns matter from organisms to the environment and back. Cycles are **gaseous** (reservoir in the atmosphere — carbon, nitrogen) or **sedimentary** (reservoir in rocks and soil — phosphorus, sulphur). The nitrogen cycle is the one with named bacterial specialists; the carbon cycle is the one we are now disturbing; the phosphorus cycle has no gas phase at all.

## 3. Classified tables

Tables carry examples in every classification and characteristics row, ≤ 12 rows, and each is referenced from the body text (§3.3).

**Concept flow — how any nutrient cycle is read (study in this order)**

| Step | Question to ask | Nitrogen example |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Where is the main reservoir? | Atmosphere (78% N2) |
| 2 | How does it enter living systems? | Nitrogen fixation by bacteria |
| 3 | How does it move through the food web? | Assimilation → plants → animals |
| 4 | How is it returned? | Ammonification from dead matter and excreta |
| 5 | How is it made reusable? | Nitrification to nitrate — the form plants take up |
| 6 | How does it leave the biosphere? | Denitrification back to N2 gas |

**Carbon vs nitrogen vs phosphorus — the three cycles compared**

| Feature | Carbon cycle | Nitrogen cycle | Phosphorus cycle |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reservoir | Atmosphere CO2 + fossil fuels + limestone | Atmosphere N2 (78%) | Rocks and phosphate ores — SEDIMENTARY |
| Gas phase | Yes (CO2, CH4) | Yes (N2) | None — no gaseous form |
| Entry to life | Photosynthesis fixes CO2 | Nitrogen fixation by bacteria | Weathering releases phosphate to soil |
| Key microbes | — | Rhizobium, Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter, Pseudomonas | Mycorrhiza helps uptake |
| Human disturbance | Fossil fuel burning → rising CO2 | Fertiliser overuse → eutrophication | Mining + detergent runoff → algal blooms |
| Speed | Fast (living) + slow (fossil) | Fast through life, slow in soil pools | Slowest of the three |

**The nitrogen cycle — each step and its named bacterium**

| Step | Change | Organism |
|---|---|---|
| Nitrogen fixation | N2 → NH3 / NH4+ | Rhizobium (nodules), Azotobacter (free-living), cyanobacteria |
| Assimilation | NH4+ / NO3− built into amino acids | Plants, then animals via food |
| Ammonification | Proteins of dead matter and urea → NH3 | Decomposer bacteria and fungi |
| Nitrification (1) | NH3 / NH4+ → NO2− | Nitrosomonas |
| Nitrification (2) | NO2− → NO3− | Nitrobacter |
| Denitrification | NO3− → N2 gas (lost to air) | Pseudomonas and anaerobic bacteria |

## 6. Key terms and statements
Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).

**Worked example — why legumes enrich soil.** A farmer rotates maize with beans. The bean roots host *Rhizobium* in nodules; the bacteria fix atmospheric N2 into ammonia the plant builds into protein. After harvest the residues decompose (ammonification), nitrifiers convert the nitrogen to nitrate, and the next maize crop takes it up. The farmer bought nitrogen with a seed instead of a fertiliser bag — the cycle did the work.

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Carbon: atmosphere ↔ photosynthesis/respiration; CO2 ~0.03–0.04% of air; largest reservoir = ocean; human addition = fossil fuels — the reservoirs in one line each.

Trick 2: Nitrogen: N2 (78% of air) unusable directly → fixation (Rhizobium, cyanobacteria, lightning) → nitrification (NH3 → NO2− → NO3−) → assimilation → denitrification (Pseudomonas back to N2) — the five stations.
Trick 3: Phosphorus: NO atmospheric phase — sedimentary cycle only; rock → soil → plants → animals → back by decomposers; slowest of the three.
Trick 4: Gaseous vs sedimentary: C and N are gaseous cycles (atmosphere reservoir), P is sedimentary (lithosphere) — the classification 2-marker.
